original_question: If X is a rationally connected manifold with pseudo-effective tangent bundle, is its anti-canonical divisor -K_X big?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact mathematical content of the paper's target open problem almost verbatim: the hypotheses are that X is rationally connected and has pseudo-effective tangent bundle, and the conclusion being asked about is whether the anticanonical divisor -K_X is big.
missing_details: In the paper's Section 4 setup, X is implicitly a smooth complex projective variety; the subsection is explicitly devoted to smooth projective varieties with pseudo-effective tangent bundle.

The phrase "pseudo-effective tangent bundle" is meant in the paper's specific sense from Proposition 4.1, not just an informal positivity condition. One equivalent formulation used there is: there exists an ample line bundle A such that A ⊗ Sym^m T_X is generically globally generated for every integer m > 0.
The quantifier is universal: the question asks whether every such X must satisfy that -K_X is big.
Rationally connected is used in the standard sense recalled in Section 2: any two points can be connected by one rational curve.
The divisor in question is the anticanonical divisor of X itself, namely -K_X, and bigness is in the usual projective-geometric sense for divisors.
refined_question: Let X be a smooth complex projective rationally connected variety whose tangent bundle T_X is pseudo-effective in the sense that there exists an ample line bundle A on X such that A ⊗ Sym^m T_X is generically globally generated for every integer m > 0. Must the anticanonical divisor -K_X be big?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if X is a smooth complex projective rationally connected variety such that the non-nef locus of O_{P(T_X)}(1) is not dominant over X, must -K_X be big?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 4 rather than any other part of the paper. Section 4 is devoted to smooth projective varieties with pseudo-effective tangent bundle, Proposition 4.1 gives the exact meaning of pseudo-effectivity and explicit equivalent formulations, and Theorem 4.2 explains the surrounding MRC-fibration context. Immediately after contrasting the pseudo-effective case with the nef tangent bundle case and observing that the Fano conclusion fails for pseudo-effective tangent bundles because of Hirzebruch-surface examples, the paper states exactly Problem 4.4: whether a rationally connected manifold with pseudo-effective tangent bundle has big anticanonical divisor. So the refined question should stay exactly at that scope and not be broadened to compact Kähler variants or neighboring MRC-fibration questions.
